title: 汇率暴跌，物价疯涨：聊聊日本十年间的物价变化｜Vol.29 - 范来张口FM
title_en: Currency Crash, Prices Soaring: Japan's Price Changes Over a Decade
summary_cn: 一句话概括：两个在日本生活了十年的中国人（老范 & 雪梨），从留学时代的"6.7汇率、物价三十年不涨"，聊到今天的"汇率跌破4、物价成倍起飞"——用衣食住行的亲历账单，还原日本从"失去的三十年"通缩常态切换到"涨价时代"的荒诞撕裂感：游客觉得日本越来越便宜，而赚日元花日元的在日居民，正同时承受工资涨幅跑不赢物价、税率压顶、身份福利被抽走的四面挤压
summary_en: Two Chinese who have lived in Japan for a decade — Lao Fan and Shirley — trace their journey from the study-abroad era of a 6.7 exchange rate and thirty years of frozen prices to today's yen below 4 and prices doubling overnight. Using their own food, clothing, housing, and transport bills, they capture the surreal rift of Japan's shift from the deflationary "lost three decades" to an era of rising prices: tourists find Japan cheaper and cheaper, while residents earning and spending in yen feel squeezed from all sides — wages lagging prices, tax rates pressing down, and welfare perks being stripped away.

scenes.title_cn: 一、汇率与身份：钱的"度量衡"变了
scenes.title_en: Exchange Rate & Identity: The "Measuring Stick" for Money Has Changed
scenes.context: 汇率从 6.7 跌到 4 点几，直接改写以人民币计价的"身价表"；还聊到留学与毕业后的身份税制差异。语域：casual 亲历分享 + 数字对比。
scenes.speak: Let's start with the exchange rate. When the hosts first arrived in Japan as students, the rate was around 6, even up to 6.7, so they converted every purchase into yuan. Today it's fallen to the low 4s, and briefly approached the 3s. A monthly salary of 250,000 yen was about 15,000 yuan at 6.7, but barely more than 10,000 yuan at 4-point-something. The exchange rate isn't an abstract macro number — it directly rewrites your value chart priced in yuan. You did nothing, and your salary automatically lost 30%. For residents earning and spending in yen, daily life feels the same — until you go home or exchange money. There's also the identity shift: as students they had tax-exempt status, so every government payout included them, but after graduation, income tax, residence tax, pension, and insurance already take nearly a third of the paycheck.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：初到日本留学时汇率约6出头（高至6.7），买什么都自动换算成人民币；如今汇率跌到4点几，甚至一度逼近3字头。同样是25万日元月薪，按6.7算是1.5万人民币，按4点几只有1万出头
sentences.en: When the hosts first arrived in Japan as students, the exchange rate was around 6 — even up to 6.7 — so they automatically converted every purchase into yuan. Today it's fallen to the low 4s, and briefly approached the 3s. A monthly salary of 250,000 yen was about 15,000 yuan at 6.7, but barely more than 10,000 yuan at 4-point-something.
sentences.note: 表达提示exchange rate → 汇率；convert into yuan → 换算成人民币；the low 4s → 4点几

sentences.cn: 关键理解：汇率不是抽象的宏观数字，它直接改写以人民币计价的"身价表"——什么都没干，工资自动"少"了30%。赚日元花日元的人日常不受影响，但一回国、一换汇，落差立刻显形
sentences.en: The exchange rate isn't an abstract macro number — it directly rewrites the "value chart" priced in yuan. You did nothing, and your salary automatically shrank 30%. For people who earn and spend yen, daily life is unaffected, but the moment you go back home or exchange currency, the gap becomes visible.
sentences.note: 表达提示priced in yuan → 以人民币计价；shrink → 缩水；the gap becomes visible → 落差立刻显形

sentences.cn: 典型场景：国内同学问起月薪时的尴尬换算；看到"有人用黑钻汇率换钱、汇率3.9"的帖子时，对未来的焦虑感
sentences.en: A typical scene: the awkward math when classmates back home ask your salary; and the anxiety when you see posts about people exchanging money at a premium "black diamond" rate of 3.9.
sentences.note: 表达提示awkward math → 尴尬的换算；premium rate → 优惠汇率；exchange money → 换汇

sentences.cn: （引用）"现在4点几的汇率，就是我什么都没干，我这个工资就自动变少了30%。"
sentences.en: "At today's rate of 4-point-something, I did nothing, and my salary automatically lost 30%."
sentences.note: 表达提示automatically lose 30% → 自动少30%

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与"游客视角的便宜"是同一枚硬币的两面——汇率正是撕裂感的根源
sentences.en: Related concept: this is two sides of the same coin as the "cheap for tourists" perspective — the exchange rate is the root of the rift.
sentences.note: 表达提示two sides of the same coin → 一枚硬币的两面；rift → 撕裂感；the root of … → 根源

sentences.cn: 原因：留学时是非课税身份，政府发钱都有份——疫情3年合计领了近60万日元（全国统一10万+学校5万+各市区町村3-10万不等）；打工时赶上迅销集团闭店仍按60%-80%发薪，加上满勤勤务，一个月挣30多万日元。毕业后变成课税身份，工资条里所得税+住民税+年金+保险已占近三分之一
sentences.en: The reason: as a student she had tax-exempt status, so every government payout included her — over the three pandemic years, she received nearly 600,000 yen in total (a national 100,000 plus the school's 50,000 plus city payouts of 30,000 to 100,000). While working part-time, even when Fast Retailing closed stores, they still paid 60% to 80% of wages, and with perfect attendance she earned over 300,000 yen a month. After graduation, she became a taxpayer: income tax, residence tax, pension, and insurance already take nearly a third of her paycheck.
sentences.note: 表达提示tax-exempt status → 非课税身份；government payout → 政府发钱；paycheck → 工资条；residence tax → 住民税

paraphrase.intent: 想说「汇率直接改写了身价」
phrases: The exchange rate silently rewrote how much my salary is worth.
My paycheck shrank 30% without me doing anything.
paraphrase.chunks: rewrite the value · shrank 30% without doing anything
paraphrase.usage: 第一句偏书面分析，第二句更口语扎心

paraphrase.intent: 想说「赚日元花日元，回国才显形」
phrases: If you earn and spend in yen, nothing feels different — until you go home.
The gap only shows up when you exchange currency or return to China.
paraphrase.chunks: earn and spend in yen · the gap shows up when…
paraphrase.usage: 第一句口语化，第二句更中性

scenes.title_cn: 二、吃：通胀最先体现在胃里
scenes.title_en: Food: Inflation Shows Up in Your Stomach First
scenes.context: 大米价格翻倍、农协垄断定价、储备米投放受阻、进口米关税锁死，以及故乡纳税制度。语域：casual 生活观察 + 制度分析。
scenes.speak: Inflation shows up in your stomach first. A five-kilogram bag of rice went from about 2,000 yen to over 4,000 yen, supermarket shelves got cleaned out, and households were limited to one bag. The government released reserve rice, but the agricultural cooperative, JA, fiercely opposed it — and JA isn't just a farm organization; it also runs banks, hospitals, and insurance, making it a monopoly-level player. The price surge isn't simple supply and demand — it's a three-layer structure of monopoly pricing, blocked reserve rice release, and import substitution locked out by tariffs of 300 percent or more. And the rescue hack is the hometown tax program: turn part of your tax bill into shopping credit on designated sites, offset it next year, and only pay a 2,000-yen processing fee.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：5公斤大米从约2000日元涨到4000多日元，超市货架搬空、一个家庭限购一袋。政府放储备米应对，农协（JA）却极力反对——农协不只是农产品组织，还有银行、医院、保险，是垄断级存在
sentences.en: A five-kilogram bag of rice went from about 2,000 yen to over 4,000 yen. Supermarket shelves got cleaned out, and each household was limited to one bag. The government released reserve rice, but the agricultural cooperative, JA, fiercely opposed it — JA isn't just a farm organization; it also runs banks, hospitals, and insurance, making it a monopoly-level player.
sentences.note: 表达提示reserve rice → 储备米；agricultural cooperative → 农业合作社（农协）；monopoly → 垄断；clean out the shelves → 搬空货架

sentences.cn: 关键理解：米价上涨并非单纯供需失衡，而是"垄断定价+储备米投放受阻+进口替代被关税挡住"三重结构的结果：据说米商不敢私自降价，否则来年拿不到农协配合
sentences.en: The key insight: the rice price surge isn't simple supply-demand imbalance — it's a three-layer structure of monopoly pricing, blocked reserve rice release, and import substitution locked out by tariffs. They say rice merchants don't dare cut prices privately, or they won't get the JA's cooperation next year.
sentences.note: 表达提示supply and demand → 供需；monopoly pricing → 垄断定价；import substitution → 进口替代；be locked out → 被挡在外面

sentences.cn: 典型场景：事件过去小一年，超市里仍见不到储备米（"只在新闻里见过"）；特价3500日元/5kg的米一上架就抢空
sentences.en: A typical scene: almost a year after the incident, reserve rice still isn't visible in supermarkets — "I've only ever seen it in the news." And the discounted rice at 3,500 yen per five kilos gets snapped up the moment it hits the shelves.
sentences.note: 表达提示snap up → 抢空；discounted → 特价的；the moment it hits the shelves → 一上架就

sentences.cn: （引用）"他规定大米4000，我有良心降到2000行吗？不行。所有人的定价都必须按照农协的要求，否则到第二年不给你配合。"
sentences.en: "They set the rice price at 4,000. Can I, with a conscience, sell at 2,000? No. Everyone's pricing must follow the JA's requirements, or they won't cooperate with you next year."
sentences.note: 表达提示with a conscience → 凭良心；follow the requirements → 按规定来；cooperate → 配合

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：对比"为什么不吃中国米"——进口米关税高达300-340%，再叠加繁杂手续与机场查验，国产替代被彻底锁死
sentences.en: Related concept: compared with "why not eat Chinese rice" — imported rice faces tariffs of 300% to 340%, plus complicated procedures and airport inspections, completely locking out domestic alternatives.
sentences.note: 表达提示tariff → 关税；domestic alternative → 国产替代；lock out → 锁死

sentences.cn: 核心机制：故乡纳税制度允许把应交税额变成购物额度，在指定网站消费，第二年用于抵税；自己只需掏2000日元手续费
sentences.en: The mechanism: the hometown tax program lets you turn part of your tax bill into shopping credit, spend it on designated sites, and use it to offset taxes next year — while you only pay a 2,000-yen processing fee.
sentences.note: 表达提示hometown tax → 故乡纳税；shopping credit → 购物额度；offset tax → 抵税；processing fee → 手续费

paraphrase.intent: 想说「农协是垄断级的存在」
phrases: JA operates like a monopoly — it's not just a farm group.
The cooperative controls everything from pricing to credit.
paraphrase.chunks: operates like a monopoly · controls pricing
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白，第二句更具体

phrases: It gets snapped up the second it hits the shelves.
People grab it the moment it's stocked.
paraphrase.usage: snap up 是地道动词短语，口语常用

scenes.title_cn: 三、住与行：东京房价翻倍与租客博弈
scenes.title_en: Housing & Transport: Tokyo Prices Double and Tenant Tactics
scenes.context: 东京新房均价破亿、房价几年涨约100%、租客可以协商涨租。语域：casual 生活观察 + 租房博弈。
scenes.speak: Next, housing and transport. After the bubble burst, prices stayed flat for over thirty years, but in the last three to five years they've risen about one hundred percent — the average new Tokyo home has broken past 100 million yen. The weak yen has pulled in global property speculators, and new units sell out almost instantly. The key insight: prices rise while wages don't — a mismatch between asset-side inflation and income-side stagnation. So second-hand homes have risen more gently and become the safe harbor for first-time buyers; the hosts now only look at resale properties. And a useful tip: in Japan, rent can be renegotiated at lease renewal. Many people from China are used to just accepting a raise, but Japanese law actually leans in the tenant's favor — you can push back.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：泡沫破灭后房价平稳了三十多年，最近3-5年却涨了约100%——东京新房均价突破1亿日元；低汇率把全球炒房客吸引进来，新房"秒没"
sentences.en: After the bubble burst, prices stayed flat for over thirty years, but in the last three to five years they've risen about 100% — the average price of a new Tokyo home has broken past 100 million yen. The weak yen has pulled in global property speculators, and new units sell out almost instantly.
sentences.note: 表达提示the bubble burst → 泡沫破灭；break past 100 million → 突破1亿；property speculator → 炒房客；sell out instantly → 秒没

sentences.cn: 关键理解：房价涨而工资不涨，是"资产端通胀"与"收入端停滞"的错位。二手房涨幅相对温和，成为刚需避风港——主播们现在只看二手房
sentences.en: The key insight: prices rise while wages don't — a mismatch between asset-side inflation and income-side stagnation. Second-hand homes have risen more gently and become the safe harbor for first-time buyers; the hosts now only look at resale properties.
sentences.note: 表达提示asset-side inflation → 资产端通胀；income stagnation → 收入端停滞；safe harbor → 避风港；resale/second-hand home → 二手房

sentences.cn: 典型场景：住在千叶以为躲开了东京，结果郊区房价也水涨船高；"东京都内拥有二三十套房产"的帖子背后，是普通老百姓"根本买不起"的落差
sentences.en: A typical scene: living in Chiba, they thought they'd escaped Tokyo, but suburban prices also rose with the tide. And behind posts bragging about "owning twenty or thirty properties in Tokyo" is the gap — ordinary people simply can't afford to buy.
sentences.note: 表达提示suburban → 郊区的；rise with the tide → 水涨船高；ordinary people can't afford it → 普通人买不起

sentences.cn: （引用）"上一次这么高，还是泡沫的时候。"
sentences.en: "The last time prices were this high was the bubble era."
sentences.note: 表达提示the bubble era → 泡沫年代

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与房租上涨、停车费翻倍同源——都是地价在传导
sentences.en: Related concept: it comes from the same source as rising rents and doubled parking fees — land prices transmitting through.
sentences.note: 表达提示come from the same source → 同源；land price → 地价；transmit → 传导

sentences.cn: 原因：日本租房合同更新时可协商涨租，很多国内来的人习惯了"房东说涨就涨"直接接受——但日本法律其实偏向租客
sentences.en: The reason: in Japan, rent can be renegotiated when a lease renews. Many people from China are used to "the landlord raises it, you accept it" and just go along — but Japanese law actually leans in the tenant's favor.
sentences.note: 表达提示lease renewal → 合同续签；renegotiate → 协商重谈；lean in sb's favor → 偏向某人

phrases: Housing prices took off, but wages stayed put.
Asset inflation left incomes behind.
paraphrase.chunks: took off · stayed put · left incomes behind
paraphrase.usage: took off / stayed put 很口语，适合聊天

paraphrase.intent: 想说「法律其实偏向租客」
phrases: The law is actually on the tenant's side.
Renters have more leverage than they think.
paraphrase.chunks: on the tenant's side · have leverage
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白，第二句更有策略感

scenes.title_cn: 四、衣与政策：从"价格锚定"到"签证门槛"
scenes.title_en: Clothing & Policy: From "Price Anchoring" to Visa Hurdles
scenes.context: 基本款牛仔裤从两三千涨到4999，心理冲击来自价格锚点；优衣库全球化定价与网购退换货的坑。语域：casual 生活观察 + 消费心理。
scenes.speak: Now clothing and policy. Basic jeans that used to cost two to three thousand yen now run 4,999 yen, and shirts went from 1,999 to 3,999. But beyond the price increase itself, the real psychological shock comes from the price anchor — your mind has decided a basic item should be worth two to three thousand, so past four thousand it's simply not worth it. GU's current prices are exactly where Uniqlo used to be, so the value-for-money mindset has shifted wholesale. It also connects to Uniqlo's global pricing strategy — prices up in Japan, down in China, the gap flattened out — which ended the era of cross-border resellers. And when shopping online, Taobao and Shein have tempting prices, but sizing is non-standard and returns are expensive in Japan, so a wrong fit means the money is sunk.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：基本款牛仔裤曾两三千日元，如今4999日元；衬衣从1999涨到3999。涨价本身之外，真正的心理冲击来自"价格锚点"——心里认定基本款就该值两三千
sentences.en: Basic jeans that used to cost two to three thousand yen now run 4,999 yen; shirts went from 1,999 to 3,999 yen. Beyond the price increase itself, the real psychological shock comes from the price anchor — your mind has decided a basic item should be worth two to three thousand.
sentences.note: 表达提示price anchor → 价格锚点；basic item → 基本款；psychological shock → 心理冲击

sentences.cn: 关键理解：涨价改写消费决策逻辑：不是"买不起"，而是"超过锚点就不值"。GU现在的价格正好是当年优衣库的价格，于是性价比心智整体转移
sentences.en: The key insight: price increases rewrite how you decide — it's not "I can't afford it," it's "past the anchor point, it's not worth it." GU's current prices are exactly where Uniqlo used to be, so the value-for-money mindset has shifted wholesale.
sentences.note: 表达提示anchor point → 锚点；value for money → 性价比；shift wholesale → 整体转移

sentences.cn: 典型场景：毕业时用社员折扣买的GU衣服一直穿到今天；快时尚网购（Shein等）一件一两千日元、设计好看但品质一般
sentences.en: A typical scene: the GU clothes she bought with an employee discount at graduation are still being worn today. Fast-fashion e-commerce like Shein sells pieces for one to two thousand yen — good-looking designs, but mediocre quality.
sentences.note: 表达提示employee discount → 员工折扣；fast fashion → 快时尚；mediocre quality → 品质一般

sentences.cn: （引用）"在你意识里面已经认定了，这个基本款就应该是两三千块钱。如果是四千以上，你就觉得没必要了。"
sentences.en: "In your mind, you've already decided the basic item should be two to three thousand. If it's over four thousand, you feel it's not worth it."
sentences.note: 表达提示not worth it → 没必要/不值

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与优衣库"日本涨价、国内降价、价差被拉平"的全球化定价策略联动——代购的时代因此落幕
sentences.en: Related concept: it connects to Uniqlo's global pricing strategy — prices up in Japan, down in China, the gap flattened out — which ended the era of cross-border resellers.
sentences.note: 表达提示global pricing strategy → 全球化定价策略；cross-border reseller / daigou → 代购；flatten the gap → 拉平价差

sentences.cn: 原因：淘宝/Shein款式多、199包邮很诱人，但版型与size不标准；在日本退换货成本高，基本买定离手，不合适就砸手里
sentences.en: The reason: Taobao and Shein offer tons of styles and tempting 199-yuan free shipping, but the fit and sizing are non-standard; in Japan, returns are expensive, so you basically buy and own — if it doesn't fit, the money is sunk.
sentences.note: 表达提示free shipping → 包邮；sizing → 尺码；buy and own → 买定离手；money is sunk → 砸手里

phrases: Once it passes your anchor price, it stops feeling worth it.
Past the mental threshold, it's no longer a "yes."
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白，第二句更抽象

paraphrase.intent: 想说「买定离手，不合适就砸手里」
phrases: You buy it and it's yours — returns aren't worth it.
No easy returns, so a wrong size is money down the drain.
paraphrase.chunks: buy it and it's yours · money down the drain
paraphrase.usage: money down the drain 是很地道的口语表达

scenes.title_cn: 五、省钱方法论：积分、比价与半价
scenes.title_en: Money-Saving Playbook: Points, Price Comparison, and Half-Price Deals
scenes.context: 日本积分体系像"第二货币"、多超市分头采购、晚上蹲半价便当。语域：casual 省钱攻略 + 方法论。
scenes.speak: The money-saving playbook. Japan's points ecosystem is massive: different apps can be linked to different credit cards, so people research which app-plus-card-plus-store combo is most profitable, then use points at checkout. The key insight: as prices rise, points become a "second currency" that only grows more valuable — some people literally live off their points, stacking up millions of them, with a quality of life that might even beat ours. The host has set her sights on being a "million-points" player, treating points research like a family finance project. And when shopping, don't lock into one supermarket: eggs, meat, and shrimp at Costco; Chinese ingredients at specialty stores; frozen vegetables and canned goods at business supermarkets; and half-price bentos at night. It's all an information-gap dividend — it rewards people who study the system.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：日本积分体系庞大：不同APP可绑定不同信用卡，研究"什么APP+什么卡+在什么店"组合最划算，结账时用积分抵扣
sentences.en: Japan's points ecosystem is massive: different apps can be linked to different credit cards, so people research which "app plus card plus store" combo is most profitable, then use points at checkout.
sentences.note: 表达提示points ecosystem → 积分体系；combo → 组合；checkout → 结账

sentences.cn: 关键理解：积分是伴随物价上涨越来越值钱的"第二货币"——有人甚至靠积分生活、攒下几百万积分，生活品质不降反升
sentences.en: The key insight: as prices rise, points become a "second currency" that grows more valuable — some people literally live off their points, stacking up millions of them, and their quality of life goes up instead of down.
sentences.note: 表达提示second currency → 第二货币；live off → 靠…生活；stack up → 攒下

sentences.cn: 典型场景：结账必问"能积分吗"；主播立志做"百万积分"玩家，把研究积分当成家庭理财项目
sentences.en: A typical scene: they always ask "can I use points?" at checkout, and the host has set her sights on being a "million-points" player, treating points research like a family finance project.
sentences.note: 表达提示set one's sights on → 立志做…；family finance → 家庭理财

sentences.cn: （引用）"有一些厉害的人甚至有上百万的积分，天天就耗这些积分去生活，生活的品质可能比我们还好。"
sentences.en: "Some impressive people hold millions of points and live off them day by day — their quality of life might even be better than ours."
sentences.note: 表达提示impressive people → 厉害的人；live off points → 靠积分生活

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与故乡纳税、半价便当同属"信息差红利"——都在奖励研究制度的人
sentences.en: Related concept: together with the hometown tax and half-price bento boxes, this is the "information-gap dividend" — it all rewards people who study the system.
sentences.note: 表达提示information gap → 信息差；dividend → 红利；bento box → 便当

sentences.cn: 核心机制：不锁定一家超市，而是把高频清单拆开：鸡蛋肉虾去Costco、中国食材去物产店集中采购、冷冻蔬菜罐头去业务超市、晚上蹲超市半价便当和熟食
sentences.en: The mechanism: don't lock into one supermarket — split the high-frequency list: eggs, meat, and shrimp at Costco; Chinese ingredients in bulk at specialty stores; frozen vegetables and canned goods at business supermarkets; and hunt half-price bentos and deli at night.
sentences.note: 表达提示specialty store → 物产店；business supermarket → 业务超市；half-price bento → 半价便当

paraphrase.intent: 想说「积分成了第二货币」
phrases: Points have become a second currency that beats inflation.
With prices rising, points only get more valuable.
paraphrase.usage: 第一句更夸张有画面，第二句更平实

paraphrase.intent: 想说「分头采购，各取所长」
phrases: Split your list across stores — each one has its specialty.
Don't stick to one shop; play each store's strength.
paraphrase.chunks: split your list across stores · play each store's strength
paraphrase.usage: 第二句 play … strength 更口语自然

scenes.title_cn: 六、撕裂感：同一片东京，两种物价
scenes.title_en: The Rift: Two Prices in the Same Tokyo
scenes.context: 游客视角的便宜与居民视角的成本上升，日本人自己也转向低消费地。语域：casual 播客总结 + 观察点评。
scenes.speak: Finally, the rift: two prices in the same Tokyo. Yen depreciation is a discount for tourists and daigou who earn foreign currency and spend yen — saving 30% to 40% — but for residents earning and spending yen it brings no real benefit. Price rises feel invisible to tourists in the short run, but for residents they show up in every monthly bill. Exchange rate plus inflation stack up, squeezing both foreigners and locals in Japan. As the host says, Tokyo today has this surreal rift — for tourists, everything is so cheap; but for us foreigners living here, the cost of living and the pressure are both rising. And Japanese people are also voting with their feet, turning to lower-cost domestic trips to Okinawa, Kyushu, and Hokkaido instead of going abroad.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：日元贬值对"赚外币花日元"的游客/代购是折扣（省30-40%），对"赚日元花日元"的居民没有实际好处；物价上涨对游客短期无感，对居民是每月账单。汇率+通胀叠加，在日外国人和日本本地人一起被挤压
sentences.en: Yen depreciation is a discount for tourists and daigou who earn foreign currency and spend yen — saving 30% to 40% — but for residents earning and spending yen it brings no real benefit. Price rises feel invisible to tourists in the short run, but for residents they show up in every monthly bill. Exchange rate plus inflation stack up, squeezing both foreigners and locals in Japan.
sentences.note: 表达提示depreciation → 贬值；discount → 折扣；stack up → 叠加；squeeze → 挤压

sentences.cn: （引用）"现在的东京就有一种特别荒诞的撕裂感：对于游客来说，日本的东西好便宜呀；对于咱们生活在日本的外国人来说，生活成本和压力都在上升。"
sentences.en: "Tokyo today has this surreal rift: for tourists, things in Japan are so cheap! But for us foreigners living here, the cost of living and the pressure are both rising."
sentences.note: 表达提示surreal rift → 荒诞的撕裂感；cost of living → 生活成本

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：日本人也在用脚投票——国内游转向冲绳、九州、北海道等低消费地，替代出境游
sentences.en: Related concept: Japanese people are also voting with their feet — domestic travel to lower-cost places like Okinawa, Kyushu, and Hokkaido is replacing overseas trips.
sentences.note: 表达提示vote with one's feet → 用脚投票；domestic travel → 国内游；replace overseas trips → 替代出境游

paraphrase.intent: 想说「游客觉得便宜，居民觉得贵」
phrases: The same Tokyo is cheap for tourists and expensive for residents.
Two groups, two price tags, one city.
paraphrase.chunks: cheap for tourists · expensive for residents · one city
paraphrase.usage: 第二句是总结式金句，适合点评

phrases: People are voting with their wallets.
Households are shifting their spending to cheaper regions.
paraphrase.chunks: voting with their wallets · shift spending to cheaper regions
paraphrase.usage: 第一句口语，第二句偏书面

practice.cn: 用「exchange rate」说：汇率从6.7跌到4点几，工资自动少了30%。
practice.en: The exchange rate fell from 6.7 to the low 4s — my salary automatically lost 30%.

practice.cn: 用「monopoly」说：农协不是普通组织，而是垄断级的存在。
practice.en: JA isn't just a farm group — it operates like a monopoly that controls pricing.

practice.cn: 用「price anchor」说：超过锚点，就觉得不值了。
practice.en: Once the price passes your anchor point, it stops feeling worth it.

practice.cn: 用「vote with their feet」说：日本人用脚投票，转向低消费地。
practice.en: Japanese people are voting with their feet, turning to lower-cost destinations.

pitfalls.wrong: The price of rice rose very fast, my heart feels broken.
pitfalls.right: The price of rice doubled — and shoppers felt the sting immediately.
pitfalls.why: 中式口语硬译情绪；英文里价格暴涨用 soared / doubled，配合 felt the sting 表达感受更地道。

pitfalls.wrong: JA is a monopolistic organization, very strong.
pitfalls.right: JA operates like a monopoly — it runs banks, hospitals, and insurance too.
pitfalls.why: monopolistic organization 太干瘪；用 operate like a monopoly 并补具体证据，才有说服力。

pitfalls.wrong: The exchange rate is very low, I am very sad.
pitfalls.right: With the exchange rate in the low 4s, my salary is worth a third less in yuan.
pitfalls.why: 直译情绪词很空；把情绪转成事实对比（worth a third less）才地道。

pitfalls.wrong: I want to buy clothes but the price is too expensive.
pitfalls.right: The price has passed my anchor point, so it no longer feels worth it.
pitfalls.why: too expensive 是中式直译；用价格锚点（anchor point / not worth it）表达消费心理判断更地道。

shifts.before: 汇率是新闻里的宏观数字，跟自己没关系
shifts.after: 汇率直接改写你的身价表——没做什么，工资就自动缩水30%
要看到垄断定价、储备受阻、进口关税三重结构，涨价背后也有"制度"
拆开高频清单分头采购 + 研究积分，是奖励会研究制度的人
